item.title: Overview
item.description:
Observability tools#

This page is for anyone who reads data from a materialize-monitoring install, and for the operators who decide who gets access. Every tool in this section reads the same metrics, logs, and alerts. The tools differ in who they suit, what access they need, and how much they ask of you.

Compare the tools#

The following table classifies each tool. Each tool’s page carries the same classification at its top.

item.title: Grafana in a browser
item.description:
Grafana in a browser#

This page is for anyone who reads Materialize monitoring through Grafana’s web UI. The bundled Grafana is where every other tool in this section starts from: the dashboards, the data sources, and the alerting views are already provisioned there.

Interface Browser
Audience Everyone who reads dashboards
Cluster access Port-forward, if Grafana isn’t exposed
Grafana access Browser login
Ease of use Highest: nothing to install
Stability Stable

Reach Grafana#

How you reach Grafana depends on whether your install exposes it:

item.title: Grafana MCP server
item.description:
Grafana MCP server#

This page is for operators and on-call engineers who want an AI agent, such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop, or Cursor, to read Materialize monitoring. The Grafana MCP server, mcp-grafana, connects an agent to Grafana over the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The agent can then search and read dashboards, run PromQL and LogQL through Grafana’s data sources, and read alerts, without Kubernetes access.

Interface AI agent, over MCP
Audience Operators who work with an AI agent
Cluster access Port-forward, if Grafana isn’t exposed
Grafana access Service account token
Ease of use High after setup, but check its answers
Stability Fast-moving: tools change in minor releases

The shipped dashboards use Grafana’s v2 dashboard schema, which mcp-grafana reads and writes natively from version 0.16.0. Use a 2.x release, which fixes several v2 bugs, including one that let update_dashboard replace a v2 dashboard with a v1 body. An older version converts each dashboard to the v1 schema before the agent sees it, which drops the panel queries in v2-only layouts.

item.title: gcx
item.description:
gcx#

This page is for operators who want Grafana from a terminal, and for anyone wiring Grafana into a script or an AI agent. gcx is Grafana Labs’ command-line tool, and it supports Grafana 13 and later. It reaches dashboards, data sources, and alerting through Grafana’s API, so it needs a Grafana login and no Kubernetes access.

Interface Command line
Audience Operators, scripts, and agents with a shell
Cluster access Port-forward, if Grafana isn’t exposed
Grafana access Service account token
Ease of use Moderate: PromQL and LogQL
Stability Stable within a major version

Connect to your Grafana#

gcx keeps each Grafana it talks to as a named context.

item.title: Backend APIs
item.description:
Backend APIs#

This page is for operators with Kubernetes access to the monitoring namespace. Thanos Query, Loki, and Alertmanager each serve an HTTP API, and you can reach each one with kubectl without going through Grafana. Use this path when Grafana is down, when the stack itself is what you’re debugging, or when a script needs the raw API.

Interface HTTP API
Audience Operators debugging the stack
Cluster access Port-forward or exec in each backend’s namespace
Grafana access None
Ease of use Lowest: kubectl, and PromQL or LogQL
Stability Stable upstream APIs

Before you start#

The backends have no authentication of their own, so anyone who can reach one reads everything it serves. Reach them through kubectl, and never through an ingress. For more information, see Securing.
